tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a larger disk that needs to be moved is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that are on top of it to other pegs, making the larger disk accessible.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk but it is blocked by smaller disks on the same peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 sits on top of it, resulting in an illegal move because the source top does not match the intended disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before executing a move, verify that the disk you intend to move is actually the topmost disk on the source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you plan to make.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, causing a source‑top mismatch error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the destination peg is either empty or its topmost disk is larger than the disk being moved, so that a larger disk is never placed on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For every move you plan to make.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place disk 5 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 3, which is smaller and therefore illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use the recursive algorithm: to move k disks from source to target, first move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, then move the kth (largest) disk, then move the k‑1 disks from auxiliary to target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a systematic, near‑optimal sequence for moving a stack of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generating an overly long move list without recursion, which exceeds the token limit and gets truncated.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg has a smaller disk on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere before moving the larger disk onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever the destination peg's top disk is smaller than the disk you want to move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 onto a peg where disk 3 is on top, without first relocating disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg without restriction, making it ideal for temporarily freeing pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary holder and the smallest disk is available.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to use a larger disk as a placeholder, which then blocks later moves because of size constraints.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Place move list as the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Output the move list as the very last list in the response, without any surrounding text, code fences, or extra characters, so the parser reads the correct list.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to capture the wrong (or empty) list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Keep move list concise to avoid token limit truncation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a short, near‑optimal sequence (e.g., using recursion) rather than an overly long list, to stay within token limits and avoid truncation.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move list, especially for larger numbers of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing a move list that is cut off by the token limit, resulting in an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure non‑empty move list when moves are required
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the initial configuration does not already match the goal, the generated move list must contain at least one move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the problem requires any change from the initial state.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Returning an empty move list for a problem where disks need to be rearranged.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Temporarily relocate out‑of‑order disks from the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a disk that belongs on the goal peg is already there but larger disks still need to be placed below it, move that disk to another peg first; after the larger disks are placed, move it back onto the goal peg in the correct order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already contains some disks, but the largest required disk for the final stack is not yet present, and a smaller disk is occupying the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to place the largest disk onto the goal peg while a smaller disk that should be placed later is already on that peg, causing an illegal placement or incorrect final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generation early or think the initial state already matches the goal, leading to no moves being emitted.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify whether the initial configuration differs from the goal; if it does, generate at least one legal move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated move list exceeds the model's output length, causing the tail to be cut off and resulting in an incomplete sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move list concise (e.g., use recursion to produce near‑optimal sequences) and monitor token usage to stay within limits.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to update the current state after previous moves or neglects to check the source peg's top before moving.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg for every move, updating the state after each move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook the size constraint on the destination peg, especially when focusing on freeing a peg for a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before executing a move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds explanatory text, code fences, or another list after the move list, which the verifier interprets as the final answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Place the move list as the very last token sequence in the response, with no trailing characters or additional lists.
